tasks.short: Address performance problems through disciplinary action

steps.what: Review performance evidence, disciplinary rules and delegated authority
Hear the employee's account and discuss the performance concern
Decide a proportionate action within delegated authority
Write the disciplinary notice and employee case entry
outputs: disciplinary notice draft and case entry

steps.what: Check final notice, evidence, wording, authority and employee destination
inputs: disciplinary notice draft and case entry
outputs: final checked disciplinary notice and employee destination

steps.what: Issue the checked disciplinary notice to the employee
inputs: final checked disciplinary notice and employee destination

tasks.design: Use the approved native {HCM} notice layout for fixed headings and employee identity. The supervisor hears the employee, decides within actual authority and writes the substantive account; the final checked notice is issued in a separate step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Disciplinary fairness requires context and an employee response.
tasks.enabler_now: Native notice structure can remove limited repeated formatting and identity entry.
tasks.still_hard: Fairness, disputed evidence and staying within delegated powers.
tasks.human_edge: Hear the employee and judge a proportionate response.
tasks.altitude: No change to disciplinary authority; a small amount of form setup is shorter.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: approved employee notice templates can reuse fixed structure; disciplinary judgement and employee hearing remain human.

assumptions: Boundary is an action the supervisor is already authorised to take, including its actual notice and case entry. Shares are provisional; dismissal or an action needing HR approval requires that real approver step and time before release.

HR supplies current policy and employee identity in {HCM}; the supervisor checks evidence in s1, hears the account in s2 and writes factual details in s4. No unpriced recording or automatic interpretation of testimony is assumed.

Test native approved form first. Only fixed notice layout and existing identity reuse, 7% of s4, are removed. Case facts, response, wording and ordinary same-system save remain fully retained and ungated.
s5 checks the final completed notice and exact employee destination before s6 issues it; edits void approval. The issue is a real formal handoff, not a relabelled save, and earns no saving.
unknowns: Actual delegated authority and HR approval rules
research_questions: Does the approved native form remove any repeated setup beyond today's template?

already_counted.description: Evidence, hearing, decision, factual writing and final notice checks remain.

incremental.description: Supervisor checks form currency with HR after policy changes.

approvals.approved_version: s5 final notice, action and exact employee destination after authority check; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 15*0.07=1.05 setup hours removed less 0.35 upkeep gives 0.7 net. Cautious case: disputed facts require bespoke notice structure, leaving only 0.4 identity-entry hours removed and 0.05 net; no hearing or decision saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Investigate employee complaints and resolve workplace problems

steps.what: Read applicable complaint procedure and management rules
Hear employee accounts and investigate relevant events
Write the existing complaint case account and unresolved factual issues
Judge the complaint and agree a permitted resolution with employees
Enter and check the agreed resolution in the complaint case

tasks.design: Configure the existing {HCM} complaint form to carry the original case identifier and fixed account fields into the investigation entry. Keep account capture, impartial investigation, resolution discussions and final case completion human; no model evaluates allegations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Conflicting accounts and confidentiality limit automatic summarisation or resolution.
tasks.enabler_now: Native case context can remove a small repeated identifier entry.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing credibility, protecting confidentiality and identifying cases requiring independent escalation.
tasks.human_edge: Listen impartially and recognise power imbalances.
tasks.altitude: No new complaint decision rights; a little less repeated case identification.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: existing employee case forms can reuse case identifiers while preserving manual factual accounts and resolution records.

assumptions: Boundary includes an existing complaint case read by HR and authorised management. Verify the real case record and provisional shares; do not add an unused complaint log.

The employee produces the complaint, HR maintains the case identifier and procedure, and the supervisor obtains accounts in s2 and writes them in s3. No free transcription or structured witness statement is assumed.

Test native {HCM} case context. Only repeated case identification, 4% of s3, is removed; all factual wording, checking and ordinary saves remain. s5 occurs after resolution, so no future decision is used earlier.

This is an informal resolution within existing authority. A formal determination letter, external referral or binding personnel change must have its own final-version approval and separate issue/activation, with actual approver labour; none is hidden in these conversations.
unknowns: Actual case-record readership and access rights
Whether a formal written determination is required
research_questions: Can original case context remove identifier re-entry without exposing confidential data?

already_counted.description: Accounts, disputed facts, resolution and final recording remain.

incremental.description: Supervisor checks complaint-form context and permissions after changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 20*0.04=0.8 identifier hours removed less 0.25 upkeep gives 0.55 net. Cautious case: a multi-employee complaint requires separate case checking, leaving 0.3 hours of context reuse and 0.05 net; no factual or resolution work shrinks.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe appearance and evaluate service performance

steps.what: Read current appearance and service-performance specifications
Observe workers' appearance and actual service performance
Evaluate compliance and discuss corrections with workers

tasks.design: Keep floor observation and contextual evaluation human, supported by the current {DOCS} standard. The standard is already available in this boundary; a new checklist or monitoring record is not created to manufacture a saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Appearance and service quality require contextual, fair observation.
tasks.enabler_now: No established software change replaces that work.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing individual performance from workload, accessibility or equipment problems.
tasks.human_edge: Give proportionate feedback without unfairly judging personal traits.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: live service observation and feedback rely on contextual human judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is routine floor observation and immediate feedback, not formal appraisal. Provisional allocations are not measured time.
Management supplies current criteria, read in s1; observed behaviour is produced in s2. No structured monitoring data is assumed.

First writes and lookups were checked separately: the standard read is explicit, but no routine observation record is established. If actual appraisal entries are required, split their first write and test native templates before assigning savings. Do not invent a trailing performance log.
Native standard access is already present and removes no established work. No system change means no upkeep.
unknowns: Whether actual observations must be entered into a formal appraisal record
research_questions: Does routine floor observation create a record that anyone uses today?

already_counted.description: Criteria reading, observation and feedback stay fully retained.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All focal work remains. A difficult service encounter retains the full contextual observation and feedback; no invented appraisal entry or camera capability supplies a saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Review current bookings, worker availability and service constraints
Choose and enter service assignments on the existing work board
Check final service assignments and assigned workers
Release the checked assignments to the assigned workers
Direct workers and resolve live service priorities

tasks.design: Use native booking-context links in the service-booking and assignment category {OTHER} to avoid retyping booking references into the existing work board. The supervisor retains assignment choices, final checks, release and live direction; no staff ranking or automatic allocation is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Booking detail may be retyped while assignments require knowledge of the workers and clients.
tasks.enabler_now: Native booking-linked entries can reuse existing identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing service delays, worker capability and customer expectations.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve competing needs and explain changes fairly.
tasks.altitude: A little less board entry; unchanged worker coordination rights.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native booking-linked work boards can reuse references without deciding worker assignments.

assumptions: Boundary is coordinating current service work, including the existing board used by workers. It is not shift-roster creation. Shares are provisional.

Reception maintains booking identifier, service, appointment time and client requirements; workers or scheduling staff maintain availability. s1 checks these sources and manually resolves gaps. s2 still chooses workers and enters task-specific instructions.
Test native booking-linked entry first. Only repeated booking references, 9% of s2, are removed; assignment judgement and ordinary internal save remain fully retained without self-gates.

s3 checks the completed assignments and exact workers before s4 releases them. This is a real assignment handoff, fully retained; edits void approval. No new behavioural staff profiling or unpriced data capture is assumed.
research_questions: Can booking context remove references without changing how workers are selected?

already_counted.description: Workload checks, assignment decisions, final checks and live direction remain.

incremental.description: Supervisor checks booking links after service or board changes.

approvals.approved_version: s3 final assignment set, booking references and exact assigned workers; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 20*0.09=1.8 re-entry hours removed less 0.4 upkeep gives 1.4 net. Cautious case: walk-in services lack booking references, leaving 0.5 hours of existing-reference reuse and 0.1 net; worker decisions and directions remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Small record-setup improvements leave people decisions and live supervision with the supervisor.
role.ambitious_version: No broader personnel authority follows from these small administrative changes.
